description.to:
Outcome: The projection lease is keyed by the site bucket name (src/papyrus_content/projection/lease.py; table papyrus-projection-locks), so on a shared bucket every tenant would wait on one lock and one busy tenant would block all. Key it by "<bucket>#<tenant>". Background projection work (the page-refresh re-render task, the home-page snapshot, the reader snapshot, full re-projections after a release) moves from direct asynchronous Lambda invokes to one queue with the tenant as the message group, so a tenant with a large re-render cannot hold the workers while others wait (Amazon SQS fair queues or FIFO groups, chosen with a measurement). A release that re-projects every tenant goes through the same queue, oldest-first.

Touches (verified at origin/develop 23fabe1d): src/papyrus_content/projection/lease.py, amplify/publication/projection-lease.ts, content-actions task scheduling (page-refresh-rerender, reader-snapshot, home-page snapshot trigger in amplify/plugins/home-page), amplify/publication/reproject-on-deploy.ts, a new queue in the shared stack.

Acceptance (Gherkin feature file: features_backend/tenant-fair-projection.feature):
Scenario: One tenant's big re-render does not delay another's publish
    Given "alpha" queued a full re-render of 3,000 pages
    When "beta" publishes one story
    Then beta's page is written without waiting for alpha's re-render to finish

Scenario: Two projections of one tenant never overlap
    Given a projection of "alpha" holds its lease
    When another projection of "alpha" starts
    Then it waits and "beta" is unaffected

Dependencies: blocked by PPY-99e309. Blocks PPY-f40a02, PPY-4a79f9. (Also recorded as kbs dependencies.)
Implements or extends: -.

Testing: pytest for the lease key; a staging load test (I_LOAD) with one noisy tenant.
Rollout: Releasable alone (the dedicated key is unchanged: no tenant means the bucket alone).
Risk and mitigation: Risk: queue ordering changes publish latency. Mitigation: publish-time single-page projection stays synchronous in the request; only bulk work is queued.

Releasable on its own: yes.
DynamoDB index: none.
AppSync authorisation: unchanged.
Design note: docs/plans/multi-tenant-architecture.md (PR on branch docs/multi-tenant-architecture).
